items.t: Eni stock: Company confirms GBP 11 billion UK investment plan
sum: Eni confirmed on Wednesday, November 11, a GBP 11 billion gross investment programme in the United Kingdom for 2026 through 2030. The announcement followed a meeting between Chief Executive Claudio Descalzi and UK Secretary of State for Energy Security and Net Zero Miatta Fahnbulleh, according to chemXplore.

Eni said around two-thirds of the planned spending is allocated to lower-carbon sectors. The portfolio includes carbon capture and storage, offshore wind and fusion initiatives alongside North Sea oil and gas activities.

Eni CCUS Holding is developing the Liverpool Bay project, which is intended to support the HyNet industrial decarbonisation cluster in North West England and North Wales. The project is expected to support more than 2,000 construction jobs and about 300 permanent positions over more than 25 years of operation.

The programme also covers the Bacton carbon capture project, offshore wind interests held through Plenitude and its participation in Vårgrønn, as well as fusion work with the UK Atomic Energy Authority. Eni retains upstream exposure in the North Sea following the combination of its UK assets with Ithaca Energy in 2024.
Eni stock traded at 26.04 euros on Lang & Schwarz at 11:39 CET on Saturday, November 14.

Eni stock: Maritime outlook trims synthetic-fuel expectations
sum: Eni's maritime strategy gained a new reference point on Wednesday, November 11, when Eni, Fincantieri and RINA presented the second edition of their Sustainable Maritime Transport Outlook in Rome. The Eni press release says the study was developed with technical support from Bain & Company Italy.

The outlook compares fuel and technology options by emissions potential, maturity, infrastructure availability and total cost of ownership through 2050. Its reference scenario projects an 80% reduction in Europe's emissions intensity from 2020 levels by 2050, while the global reduction is projected at 40%.

The updated assessment is more cautious than the previous edition. Eni said the projected contribution of synthetic fuels to Europe's decarbonization pathway has been reduced by around half, reflecting weaker momentum in the low-emission hydrogen supply chain and greater uncertainty around regulation, macroeconomic conditions, fuel availability and infrastructure.

The change also affects the investment picture. Estimated European port infrastructure upgrades are now placed at 15 billion US dollars, compared with roughly 25 billion US dollars in the previous outlook. Biofuels, fossil and bio-LNG are expected to form the backbone of Europe's 2050 fuel mix, while synthetic fuels remain important for the longer-term net-zero pathway.

For Eni, the report links the company's Enilive biofuel business with a wider maritime transition in which existing vessels and infrastructure can support lower-emission fuels. The company said stable rules, reliable fuel volumes and clearer price signals will be needed to unlock investment.
Eni stock traded at 25.97 euros on Lang & Schwarz at 17:07 CET on Friday, November 13, 2026.

Eni stock: Maritime report highlights decarbonization options
sum: Eni, Fincantieri and RINA presented the second edition of the Sustainable Maritime Transport Outlook in Rome on Thursday, November 12, 2026. The report examines how shipping can reduce emissions while companies and regulators weigh technology, fuel availability and investment requirements.

The Port Journal, republishing material from The Maritime Executive, said the outlook was developed with technical support from Bain & Company Italy. It compares different technology and fuel options by emissions-reduction potential, maturity, infrastructure availability and total cost of ownership through 2050.

The analysis draws on interviews across the maritime value chain. Participating shipowners and operators represent about 40 percent of the container market and 20 percent of the cruise market, while interviewed engine and propulsion suppliers account for more than 80 percent of the internal-combustion-engine market.

The report's central message is that the outlook is more uncertain than it was a year earlier. At the same time, it identifies competitive solutions that can reduce environmental impact now, offering a practical response to European regulations while the International Maritime Organization considers global measures.

For Eni, the presentation highlights the company's role beyond oil and gas production. The company is also exposed to the development of lower-carbon fuels and energy solutions used by industrial and maritime customers. The outlook does not provide a new earnings forecast, but it frames the commercial environment in which future fuel demand and infrastructure decisions will be made.

Eni's investor page lists third-quarter 2026 adjusted EBIT of 6.0 billion euros, adjusted net profit of 2.8 billion euros and operating cash flow before working-capital changes of 4.3 billion euros. These figures provide the financial backdrop for investment decisions, although the maritime outlook itself is a strategic industry assessment rather than a results update. Further investor material is available on Eni's investor page.

Eni stock advances Cronos gas project toward first production in 2028
sum: Eni stock is in focus after Eni signed the main engineering, procurement, construction and drilling contracts for the Cronos gas project in Cyprus. The company announced the milestone on Monday, October 26, saying the contracts marked the start of the execution phase for Cyprus' first gas development.

Eni's press release said the contracts cover a floating control unit, transport and installation work, offshore pipelines, subsea production systems, flexible lines, umbilicals, an onshore pipeline and drilling services. The move followed the final investment decision reached on July 28, 2026, for the development of the Cronos discovery in Block 6 offshore Cyprus.

Cronos contains more than 3 trillion cubic feet of gas initially in place, according to Eni. The project is expected to reach a production plateau of up to 500 million standard cubic feet per day, with start-up targeted for the first half of 2028.

Eni operates Block 6 with a 50 percent interest alongside TotalEnergies. The partners plan to use a fast-track development model based on existing regional infrastructure rather than building a separate processing and liquefaction chain.

Gas from Cronos is planned to travel to Egypt for processing through existing facilities, including infrastructure associated with the Zohr field. It would then be liquefied at the Damietta LNG plant before being shipped to international markets, primarily Europe. The route links Cypriot production with Egyptian infrastructure and European gas demand.

For Eni, the project adds a new upstream development to its Eastern Mediterranean portfolio. The company has operated in Cyprus since 2013 and also operates Block 8, while holding interests in Blocks 7 and 11. The production timetable remains the next major project milestone for investors.
Eni stock traded at 25.43 euros on Lang & Schwarz at 10:40 CET on Thursday, November 12, 2026.

European ADR Selloff Hits Broad Range Of Stocks Tuesday, With Novo Nordisk (NYSE: NVO) And Eni (NYSE: E) Among Hardest Hit
sum: A broad retreat swept through European equities trading on American exchanges during Tuesday’s session, with most major American depositary receipts finishing the day in negative territory.
Novo Nordisk (NYSE: NVO) suffered one of the steeper losses among the group, with shares sliding 1.90% as selling pressure weighed on the Danish pharmaceutical giant throughout the afternoon.
Italian energy major Eni (NYSE: E) fared even worse, posting the session’s largest decline among the tracked names at 1.98%, reflecting broader weakness in European energy-linked securities.
Focal Systems (NASDAQ: FOCL) also saw meaningful losses, retreating 1.85% and adding to a pattern of softness across the European ADR landscape on the day.
Nokia (NYSE: NOK), the Finnish telecommunications equipment maker, was not spared, though its 0.43% dip was comparatively modest against the steeper drops recorded elsewhere in the group.
The one standout in an otherwise downbeat session was Banco Santander (NYSE: SAN), which managed to eke out a gain of 0.20%, bucking the broader trend affecting European names.
The divergence between Santander’s marginal advance and the losses posted by its peers underscores the uneven pressures currently facing European companies listed on American markets.

Eni stock slips 1.50 percent as buyback stays in focus
sum: Eni stock traded at 25.02 euros on Lang & Schwarz at 18:00 CET on Friday, November 6, 2026. The quote was 1.50 percent below the 25.40 euros recorded in the previous report on Thursday, November 5.

On Wednesday, November 4, Eni said it had bought 4,278,035 of its own shares on Euronext Milan between October 26 and October 30. The purchases represented 0.14 percent of share capital and carried a weighted average price of 26.8815 euros per share.

The company reported total consideration of 114,999,934.62 euros. The transactions formed part of the second tranche of the treasury-share program approved by shareholders on May 6. Eni said the program is intended to provide shareholders with additional remuneration alongside dividends.

Since the program began on May 8, Eni had acquired 93,308,523 shares for total consideration of 2,169,915,235.04 euros. Including treasury shares already held, the company reported 180,136,630 treasury shares, equal to 5.95 percent of its share capital.

The latest repurchases follow Eni's third-quarter update, which highlighted stronger operating performance and higher planned shareholder distributions. The buyback therefore adds detail to the capital-allocation plan rather than signaling a change in operating strategy.

For investors, the next focus is the pace of further repurchases and the cash-flow backdrop supporting distributions. Future returns remain sensitive to energy prices and the company's ability to sustain operating cash generation.

SLB OneSubsea wins Eni contract for Baleine Phase 3
sum: SLB Ltd.'s OneSubsea JV secured an EPC contract from Eni SpA for Phase 3 of the Baleine project, supplying subsea production systems for 13 wells offshore Côte d’Ivoire. The scope includes installation and life-of-field support, leveraging SLB's local presence. SLB shares gained 1.24% to $48.35 on Monday, trading near support levels as the energy sector outperformed the broader market.
*this image is generated using AI for illustrative purposes only.

SLB Ltd.'s OneSubsea joint venture has been awarded a major engineering, procurement, and construction (EPC) contract by Eni SpA for Phase 3 of the deepwater Baleine project offshore Côte d’Ivoire. This agreement reinforces SLB's position as a core technology and execution partner for one of the region's most strategically significant offshore developments. The stock gained over 1% on Monday following the announcement, trading at $48.35, as investors rotated into energy stocks while the broader market declined.

Under the terms of the contract, SLB OneSubsea will deliver complete subsea production systems (SPS) for 13 wells. The scope of work encompasses subsea trees, umbilicals, manifolds, multiphase flowmeters, and control systems. Additionally, the agreement includes installation, commissioning, and life-of-field support. The project will be executed through SLB's established local presence in Côte d’Ivoire to ensure efficient delivery across the project's life cycle.

The Baleine project is recognized as a strategically significant offshore development in the region. Eni stock gains as Q3 profit surge lifts cash-return outlook
sum: Eni's third-quarter performance strengthened the Italian energy group's cash-return outlook ahead of a busy industry week. In a press release published by Eni on October 23, the company said its board had approved the third-quarter and nine-month results and increased both its cash flow outlook and shareholder distributions.

Eni stock traded at 26.85 euros on Lang & Schwarz at 09:07 CET on Monday, November 2, 2026. The quote is a market indication and is not paired here with a verified Xetra closing comparison. Investors can follow the real-time quote of Eni stock during the session.

Eni said pro forma adjusted EBIT doubled year on year to 6 billion euros in the third quarter. Adjusted net profit more than doubled to 2.8 billion euros, while exploration and production delivered pro forma adjusted EBIT of 4.63 billion euros, up 76 percent from the year-earlier quarter.

Underlying upstream production rose 7 percent year on year to 1.83 million barrels of oil equivalent per day and increased 2 percent sequentially. Eni attributed the production progress to project ramp-ups in West Africa, offshore Mexico and Norway, together with a full-quarter contribution from the Searah joint venture in Southeast Asia.

Gas, global gas and power operations generated 0.45 billion euros of pro forma adjusted EBIT, including 0.41 billion euros from the gas business. Enilive's pro forma adjusted EBIT rose 80 percent to 0.41 billion euros, supported by biorefining, while Plenitude reached 0.19 billion euros, up 95 percent as renewable-energy volumes grew. Refining also benefited from improved plant utilization, although Versalis remained loss-making amid weaker chemical-product margins.

Eni raised its 2026 cash flow from operations outlook to 16.5 billion euros. The company also lifted its underlying oil and gas production growth range to 6-7 percent, increased its gas and power EBIT guidance to about 1.5 billion euros and raised the full-year Enilive pro forma adjusted EBITDA target to 1.4 billion euros.
Strong operating cash generation and portfolio actions reduced pro forma gearing to 9 percent at the end of the third quarter.

Stock markets: better-than-expected US jobs figures bring the Fed’s rate hike closer. Milan closes down 0.3 per cent
sum: The Milan Stock Exchange closed the week down 1.1 per cent. The 162,000 additional jobs in August – well above forecasts – make a rise in US interest rates more likely. Brent crude is trading at around $95 per barrel.

(Il Sole 24 Ore Radiocor) - A better-than-expected US employment report has strengthened expectations of a Fed rate rise in September and is keeping the markets on edge. Thus, whilst Wall Street closed lower, the European stock markets ended the week’s final trading session with mixed results: Milan, held back by banks and oil companies, lost 0.28 per cent to 51,100 points. Looking at the figures in detail, the US jobs report for August paints a much rosier picture than expected. Non-farm employment rose by 162,000 jobs, well above the forecast of 53,000, whilst the unemployment rate remained stable at 4.1 per cent. These figures appear to give the Federal Reserve scope to raise interest rates at this month’s meeting. Indeed, “in the Fed’s view, the labour market is holding up well, which means that inflation remains the most serious problem” to be addressed, explains Bret Kenwell of eToro. The deciding factor for the markets will be the consumer price index report, due out next Friday. Meanwhile, short-term interest rate futures now indicate a probability of around 65 per cent of a rate rise at the Fed’s next meeting, compared with around 55 per cent prior to the employment data.

The surge in crude oil prices – with Brent crude trading above $95 once again – along with inflation fears and the latest spike in global government bond yields are weighing on the weekly performance of European stock markets. Furthermore, adding to the gloom among investors during today’s session was a better-than-expected US jobs report, which has reinforced expectations of a monetary tightening by the Fed in September. As a result, European stock markets ended the week on a weak note. In particular, Paris was the worst-performing market, down 2.4%, whilst Milan (-1.1%) and Frankfurt (-0.3%) also ended the day in the red. Madrid (+0.4%), London (+0.1%) and Amsterdam (+0.8%) remained in positive territory, the latter buoyed by the strong performance of the semiconductor sector.

Eni Raises 2026 Output Forecast and Expands Share Buyback to 3.4 Billion
sum: Eni raised its 2026 oil and gas production outlook and expanded its share buyback program after reporting significantly stronger second-quarter results, supported by double-digit production growth, higher commodity prices and improved performance across several business segments.

The Italian energy company now expects underlying full-year hydrocarbon production growth of around 5%, up from its previous guidance of 3% to 4%, following 11% year-over-year underlying production growth in the second quarter to 1.79 million barrels of oil equivalent per day, excluding price effects.

The improved outlook prompted Eni to increase its planned 2026 share repurchase program to €3.4 billion, up from the previously revised €2.8 billion, while reaffirming its planned dividend of €1.10 per share. The company also said an extraordinary dividend could be considered later this year if refining margins remain well above budget assumptions.

Second-quarter adjusted EBIT more than doubled year over year to €5.38 billion, while adjusted net profit rose to €2.3 billion. The upstream business generated €4.77 billion in adjusted EBIT, benefiting from higher production, favorable oil realizations and continued cost discipline. Cash flow before working capital reached €4.47 billion, comfortably covering €1.84 billion in capital spending and €1.35 billion returned to shareholders through dividends and buybacks during the quarter.

Strategically, Eni continued expanding its upstream portfolio and transition businesses. During the quarter it established the Searah joint venture with Petronas, creating a regional platform spanning Indonesia and Malaysia that will develop major gas discoveries in the Kutei Basin. The company also approved final investment decisions for the Baleine Phase 3 development offshore Côte d'Ivoire, the Greater PAJ project offshore Angola, and the Cronos gas project offshore Cyprus.

Eni also entered the critical minerals sector through investments in graphite and lithium projects in Canada and Chile, signed an agreement with Mercuria to create a global commodities trading joint venture, and advanced plans to partially deconsolidate renewable energy business Plenitude while retaining a 65% stake.

Eni and PETRONAS launch Searah, a $20 billion 50:50 upstream joint venture covering 19 assets across Indonesia and Malaysia
sum: Eni and PETRONAS have formally launched Searah, a 50:50 joint venture combining 19 upstream oil and gas assets across Indonesia and Malaysia. The new company starts operations producing more than 300,000 barrels of oil equivalent per day and plans to deploy $20 billion in capital over the next five years. According to Wood Mackenzie, Searah has the scale and resource base to become Southeast Asia’s largest upstream producer by 2030.
Searah launches with 19 assets and immediate production above 300,000 boe/d

Searah is structured as a true 50:50 partnership—neither side holds a controlling stake. The venture spans 19 upstream assets across two of Southeast Asia’s most active hydrocarbon basins, combining producing fields in Malaysia with Eni’s deepwater gas portfolio in Indonesia’s Kutei Basin.

From day one, Searah produces more than 300,000 boe/d. That’s not a forecast — it’s the baseline. The Malaysian producing assets generate immediate cash flow and borrowing capacity, so the venture doesn’t need funding from either parent to get started.
Headquartered in London, Searah runs as a standalone company making its own investment decisions, drawing on technical support from Eni through service agreements.
Complementary portfolios drive the rationale behind the partnership

The 50:50 split reflects what each partner brings, not an equal division of reserves or cash flow. PETRONAS contributes near-term production, established infrastructure, and stable cash flows from its Malaysian assets—a financial base that supports the venture during its early years while longer-term projects get developed.

SLB OneSubsea Awarded EPC Contract for Eni’s Baleine Phase 3 Project Offshore Côte d'Ivoire
sum: Integrated subsea production system and local capabilities enable accelerated deepwater development

HOUSTON, July 13, 2026 — Global energy technology company SLB (NYSE: SLB) announced today that its OneSubsea™ joint venture has been awarded a major multi-well engineering, procurement, and construction (EPC) contract by Eni for Phase 3 of the deepwater Baleine project offshore Côte d’Ivoire.

Under the contract, SLB OneSubsea will deliver complete subsea production systems (SPS) for 13 wells, reinforcing its role as a core technology and execution partner on one of the most strategically significant offshore developments currently underway in the region.

The EPC scope includes subsea trees, umbilical, manifolds, multiphase flowmeters and control systems, along with installation, commissioning and life-of-field support. The integrated delivery model is designed to streamline execution and support the project’s fast-track development schedule.

"Baleine Phase 3 brings together scale and execution certainty," said Mads Hjelmeland, chief executive officer of SLB OneSubsea. "Through our subsea production system technology and by leveraging our established local presence, we are supporting Eni’s efforts to advance a complex, deepwater project efficiently while contributing to the long-term development of offshore resources in Côte d’Ivoire."
Project execution will be supported by SLB OneSubsea’s in-country presence and local capabilities, contributing to efficient delivery across the life of the project.
- Eni has awarded SLB OneSubsea a multi-well EPC contract for the Baleine Phase 3 development.

Record-breaking energy sector on the Milan Stock Exchange: worth 250 billion
sum: Thanks to the latest rally, the sector accounts for over 21 per cent of the total market capitalisation of the Italian stock market, led by Enel and Eni

Rising commodity prices, the issue of energy security, the growing electrification linked to AI and the green transition, generous dividends, special transactions, and the increasing industrial and financial efficiency of smaller companies. This is the mix of factors that drove the energy sector on the Milan Stock Exchange to all-time highs in the first half of the year, resulting in a total market capitalisation of 250 billion euros, without the prospect of monetary tightening (which subsequently did indeed begin) by central banks having a significant impact on the rally.

As at 1 July – according to a survey carried out by CoMar, as part of the Financial Observatory chaired by Massimo Rossi – the 18 listed energy companies accounted for 21.6 per cent of the entire Milan stock exchange (compared with 20.9 per cent at the start of the year). This increase was the result of a 13.7 per cent rally in 2026, exceeding the +10 per cent recorded by the Italian stock market as a whole, which added 30 billion to the weighting of a sector that is now increasingly strategic, both in Italy and globally, particularly in light of the ongoing geopolitical shocks, ranging from the war in Ukraine to Trump’s raid on Venezuela, right through to the US-Iran conflict involving the blockade of the Strait of Hormuz – a situation that is far from being definitively resolved.

In absolute terms, the largest share is held by the major state-owned companies, starting with Enel and Eni, which, with 101 and 62 billion respectively, account for 8.8 per cent and 5.3 per cent of the entire Milan Stock Exchange, with Snam rounding off the top three – albeit some way behind – at 20.9 billion (1.8 per cent). It is clear, in any case, that all three are to be regarded, for various reasons, as crucial companies for Italy’s energy security, but also, at the same time, as attractive investment targets for both institutional investors and large funds as well as retail investors, thanks to their financial discipline and generous dividend policies.

items.t: Eni ranks as the world’s leading company by computing power in the new TOP500 global ranking
sum: San Donato Milanese (MI), 23 June 2026 – Eni announces the launch of its new supercomputing system, HPC7 (High Performance Computing – HPC), which, with a capacity of over 861 PFlops/s, ranks 6th overall in the new TOP500 global ranking, second supercomputer in Europe and confirming its position as the world’s most powerful High-Performance Computer for industrial use. HPC7 thus surpasses HPC6, launched in November 2024, which has in turn confirmed its position within the TOP10, ranking 8th in the TOP500 list.

The combination of the HPC6 and HPC7 computing systems exceeds the Exascale threshold. Together, HPC6 and HPC7 can deliver over 1 Exaflop/s (1 Exaflop/s = 1000 PFlops/s), equivalent to more than 1 billion billion complex mathematical operations per second. The achievement of Exascale-class performance by Eni’s supercomputing system represents the attainment of the most advanced and extraordinary technological frontier in the world of supercomputing and confirms the company’s leadership in the sector.

The launch of HPC7 marks a key milestone in Eni’s strategy to enhance energy resources and decarbonization, within a model where technology is a central element of innovation, capable of supporting growth, efficiency and competitiveness in both traditional and transition businesses.

In this context, advanced computing and HPC systems are confirmed as central to Eni, enabling the integration and enhancement of expertise and applications across the entire value chain: from subsurface understanding to the optimization of industrial plant operations, as well as improving the accuracy of geological and fluid dynamics studies for CO₂ storage and the development of advanced energy technologies.

Supercomputing also contributes to accelerating the evolution of key innovation drivers, supporting the efficiency of emerging value chains – such as biofuels – and the simulation of complex phenomena, including plasma behaviour in magnetic confinement fusion.
In this framework, HPC also establishes itself as a crucial enabler for the internal development of artificial intelligence use cases in support of Eni’s businesses.

items.t: Eni Shareholders Back €4 Billion Buyback and Confirm New Board
sum: Shareholders of Italian energy major Eni approved the company's 2025 financial statements, a €4 billion share buyback program, and a new slate of directors and auditors at the company's annual meeting on Wednesday, as the group continues to prioritize shareholder returns amid volatile energy markets.
The company also confirmed a total 2026 dividend of €1.10 per share, to be distributed in four installments through May 2027, alongside authorization for a potential extraordinary dividend

Shareholders approved Eni's 2025 standalone financial statements, which showed net profit of approximately €4.43 billion, and voted to allocate the earnings to reserves rather than distribute them directly.

The meeting also renewed Eni's board for a three-year term ending with approval of the 2028 financial statements. Giuseppina Di Foggia was appointed chair of the board, while long-serving CEO Claudio Descalzi retained a board seat as the company continues to expand its upstream portfolio and low-carbon businesses.

A major focus of the meeting was shareholder remuneration. Investors authorized the repurchase of up to 303 million shares for a total consideration of up to €4 billion through April 2027, with most of the buyback earmarked for shareholder remuneration. The company also secured approval to cancel up to 297.9 million treasury shares.

The move reinforces a broader trend among European oil majors prioritizing capital returns as commodity prices stabilize after the extreme volatility seen following Russia's invasion of Ukraine. Companies including Shell plc and TotalEnergies SE have likewise maintained aggressive buyback and dividend strategies despite weaker refining margins and softer crude prices.

Eni has increasingly positioned itself as one of Europe's most active energy transition investors while continuing to grow oil and gas production. The company has expanded its upstream presence in Africa and the Eastern Mediterranean in recent years, while also advancing biofuels, carbon capture, and renewable power projects.

‘We are going to hit them hard’: Markets disappointed, oil up again after Trump speech
sum: Oil rose sharply, and US and European stocks fell after US President Donald Trump said in his first national address since the Iran war began that the US would continue to hit Iran and "finish the job".

Instead of declaring victory or offering clarity on his strategy in the Iran war, the US president promised fresh attacks over the next two to three weeks, reviving fears of rising inflation and slowing economic growth.

Dampened hopes for an end to the war in Iran weighed on stock markets worldwide and gave oil prices a fresh boost early on Thursday. In a rare move, the US benchmark, WTI crude, traded above Brent crude — the global seaborne benchmark and the one most affected by the Iran conflict so far.

“The fact that traders are now prepared to pay a premium for WTI suggests they are becoming worried about the deliverability of seaborne oil — Brent — and scrambling for what they see as a more reliable option, namely WTI,” said Russ Mould, investment director at AJ Bell.
“This, in turn, suggests traders are starting to position themselves for a conflict that is longer and more drawn out than hoped.”
Nearing 3 p.m. CET, WTI was up 11.5%, at over $111 per barrel, while Brent front-month futures traded at $108.90 per barrel, up more than 7.6%.

In his prime-time speech to Americans, Donald Trump said, “We are going to hit them extremely hard over the next two to three weeks. We’re going to bring them back to the Stone Ages, where they belong.”

EIB and Eni sign €500 million in financing for new biorefinery in Sannazzaro de’ Burgondi
sum: San Donato Milanese (Milan), 1 April 2026 - Today the European Investment Bank (EIB) and Eni signed a 15-year loan for €500 million to convert selected units of Eni’s Sannazzaro de’ Burgondi refinery, located in the Italian province of Pavia, into a biorefinery. The agreement was signed by EIB Vice-President Gelsomina Vigliotti and Eni CEO Claudio Descalzi.

The project involves converting the refinery’s Hydrocracker (HDC2) unit using Ecofining™ technology, and building a pre-treatment plant for waste materials like used cooking oils and animal fats, as well as waste from the agri-food industry, which comprise the main feedstock used by Enilive (Eni’s company devoted to achieving more sustainable mobility) to produce hydrotreated vegetable oil (HVO) biofuels.

With its proprietary Ecofining™ technology, Enilive produces HVO – a biofuel made from renewable feedstocks (pursuant to the EU Renewable Energy Directive) such as used cooking oils and waste from the agri-food industry. Pure HVO can be used in approved engines, and is already available at more than 1 600 Enilive service stations across Europe. From 2028, the Sannazzaro plant will start producing HVO diesel biofuels and the sustainable aviation fuel (SAF) biojet, with a production capacity of around 550 000 tonnes per year.

Building on existing utilities and infrastructure, the project will complement conventional fuel production with HVO diesel biofuels and SAF, helping reduce the carbon footprint of transport and decarbonise the aviation sector, for which SAF is currently the only available solution. By diversifying the product offering on the market, the project will also strengthen Italian and EU energy security, and serve the objectives of REPowerEU by expanding Europe’s biofuel production capacity.

The project follows a €500 million financing agreement signed in July 2025 to convert Eni’s Livorno refinery into a biorefinery. Transforming part of the Sannazzaro de’ Burgondi refinery as well pursues Enilive’s strategic objective: increasing biofuel production capacity to 5 million tonnes by 2030, including over 2 million tonnes of SAF production capacity.

items.t: Iran war: Europe's corporate winners and losers revealed
sum: As the conflict in Iran enters its third week, the market is telling a stark story — one of energy windfalls and industrial ruin, drawn along a single fault line: proximity to oil.
Eighteen days into the war in Iran, and the scorecard for global equity markets makes for uncomfortable reading.

European benchmark indices have shed around 7% since hostilities began — the Euro STOXX 50 down 6.5%, Germany's DAX off 7%, France's CAC 40 down 7.2%, and Italy's FTSE MIB lower by 6.4% — dwarfing the more modest 2.5% decline in the US S&P 500, which benefits from America's status as the world's largest oil producer and its relative insulation from the energy shock.
Beneath the surface, an extraordinary divide has opened up — between European companies that thrive on expensive energy, and those being crushed by it.
The conflict's most immediate economic consequence has been a seismic repricing of energy.
Iran's effective closure of the Strait of Hormuz — through which 20% of the world's petroleum flows — caused Brent crude to surge from around $70 to nearly $120 per barrel within days.
As of Tuesday, Brent sits at approximately $105, a 42% rally from pre-war levels.

items.t: Canadian Natural Resources Faces Rising Risks: Hold or Sell the Stock?
sum: Canadian Natural Resources Limited CNQ, a Canada-based oil and gas exploration and production company, has established itself as a major player in the energy sector, with a diversified portfolio spanning oil sands, natural gas and conventional crude production, which has historically delivered steady cash flows and resilience amid market fluctuations. The company’s operational scale and strong presence in Canada position it as a reliable option for investors seeking exposure to the energy market.

However, one notable concern is CNQ’s high price-to-earnings ratio of 24.73x, which exceeds the Canadian oil and gas exploration and production sub-industry average of 22.82x. This elevated valuation may reflect market optimism that outpaces the company’s realistic growth prospects, suggesting that potential investors should exercise caution, as the stock may be slightly overextended relative to its fundamental earnings potential.

While Canadian Natural Resources has a strong operational footprint and a history of stable cash flows, it is not without challenges. Investors should be aware of several factors that could impact future performance and valuation.

Significant Exposure to Volatile Commodity Prices: The company's financial performance is heavily tied to crude oil and natural gas prices, which are notoriously volatile. Realized synthetic crude oil (“SCO”) prices fell 20% in the fourth quarter of 2025 compared with the same period in 2024, directly impacting revenues and highlighting the risk of earnings declines during market downturns.

Declining International Production Volumes: CNQ’s International crude oil production dropped 52% in 2025 compared with the prior year, caused by planned maintenance, decommissioning activities and natural field declines. This significant contraction in a key operating area underscores the challenges and declining contribution from the company's non-North American assets.
Substantial Long-Term Debt and Interest Obligations: While the balance sheet is strong, the company still carries a significant long-term debt load of C$16.6 billion.
